chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day should not employ a worker until he informs him of his wages, and the one who employs a worker then withholds him from Friday (prayer) bears his sin, and if he does not withhold him, they share in the reward.

key_terms.يَبُؤُ بِإِثْمِهِ: Bears his sin / Incurs his guilt

ai.seo_question: What are the employer's obligations regarding wages and Friday prayer for a worker in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the pre-condition of wage clarity as a marker of true faith, linking spiritual belief to contractual justice. It further highlights the employer's duty to facilitate religious obligations, noting that preventing a worker from Friday prayer incurs the employer's sin, while permitting it results in shared reward, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing material rights with spiritual well-being.
